questions.question_text: Ethan receives weekly take-home pay of $\$620$. His weekly expenses are transport of $\$70$, board of $\$210$, and other spending of $\$180$. What is his annual budget balance using a $52$-week year?

options.why: Reports the weekly balance without multiplying by $52$.
Omits the weekly transport expense of $\$70$ from total expenses.
Subtracts income from expenses instead of expenses from income.

questions.question_text:
An individual has an annual net income of $\$54\,000$ and total annual expenses of $\$48\,600$.
What is their monthly budget balance?

options.why: Stops at the annual surplus of $\$5400$ and forgets to divide by $12$ to convert it to a monthly balance.
Divides correctly by $12$ but subtracts the wrong way round, taking income from expenses and so reporting the balance as a shortfall.
Subtracts income from expenses instead of expenses from income and also leaves the figure annual instead of dividing by $12$.
Calculates the monthly surplus but forgets to convert to an annual amount ($\times 12$).
Subtracts only fixed expenses from income before annualising ($(\$4200 - \$2500) \times 12$).
Multiplies monthly surplus by $26$ fortnights instead of $12$ months.

questions.question_text: A household receives monthly take-home income of $\$5100$ and has total monthly expenses of $\$4600$. What is its annual budget balance?

options.why: Reports the monthly balance without multiplying by $12$.
Subtracts income from expenses instead of expenses from income.
Multiplies the monthly balance by $52$ weeks instead of $12$ months.

questions.question_text: A worker receives monthly take-home income of $\$3300$. Their monthly fixed expenses total $\$2400$ and their monthly discretionary expenses total $\$1200$. What is their annual budget balance?

options.why: Reports the monthly deficit without multiplying by $12$.
Subtracts income from expenses and interprets the positive difference as a surplus.
Omits discretionary expenses and subtracts only fixed expenses from income.

questions.question_text:
Oliver earns $\$850$ per week. His expenses are: Rent $\$310$/week, Groceries $\$180$/week, Electricity $\$360$/quarter ($4$ quarters/year), Car running costs $\$220$/fortnight, and Entertainment $\$120$/fortnight.
What is Oliver's annual budget balance?

options.why: Omits the quarterly electricity expense from the annual total.
Calculates fortnight expenses with $\times 12$ instead of $\times 26$.
Calculates weekly rent and groceries using $48$ weeks instead of $52$.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Annual income} = \$850 \times 52 = \$44\,200$
$\text{Rent} = \$310 \times 52 = \$16\,120$
$\text{Groceries} = \$180 \times 52 = \$9360$
$\text{Electricity} = \$360 \times 4 = \$1440$
$\text{Car costs} = \$220 \times 26 = \$5720$
$\text{Entertainment} = \$120 \times 26 = \$3120$
$\text{Total annual expenses} = \$16\,120 + \$9360 + \$1440 + \$5720 + \$3120 = \$35\,760$
$\text{Annual balance} = \$44\,200 - \$35\,760$
$= \$8440\text{ surplus}$

questions.question_text: An individual receives take-home pay of $\$780$ per week. Their expenses are rent of $\$300$ per week, groceries of $\$140$ per week, transport of $\$180$ per fortnight, and other living expenses of $\$350$ per month. What is their annual budget balance?

options.why: Multiplies the fortnightly transport expense by $12$ instead of $26$.
Omits the monthly other living expenses of $\$350$ from the annual total.
Uses $48$ weeks instead of $52$ for rent and groceries while correctly using $52$ weeks for income.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Annual income} = \$780 \times 52 = \$40\,560$
$\text{Rent} = \$300 \times 52 = \$15\,600$
$\text{Groceries} = \$140 \times 52 = \$7280$
$\text{Transport} = \$180 \times 26 = \$4680$
$\text{Other living expenses} = \$350 \times 12 = \$4200$
$\text{Total annual expenses} = \$15\,600 + \$7280 + \$4680 + \$4200 = \$31\,760$
$\text{Budget balance} = \$40\,560 - \$31\,760$
$= \$8800\text{ surplus}$
